chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who struck another man with a stick, so his hearing, vision, tongue, intellect, and private parts were lost, and his ability to copulate ceased, while he was alive — (a judgement of) six wergilds.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for compensation when a single blow causes multiple bodily injuries?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the precise application of *diyah* (blood money) in Shia jurisprudence, where Imam Ali (AS) assigns a distinct compensation for each of the five major faculties lost—hearing, sight, speech, intellect, and reproductive capacity—plus an additional share for the loss of sexual function. This ruling underscores the high value placed on sensory and cognitive integrity in Islamic law, establishing a precedent for calculating compensation for compound injuries resulting from a single act. It reflects the detailed legal methodology of the Imams in addressing complex bodily damages with equitable financial restitution.
